inputs.text: The “No Kings” numbers—8 million people at more than 3,300 events across all 50 states—come from the organisers, while authorities have provided no official count. That gap is doing useful work: the headline can project overwhelming opposition without anyone independently settling the figure. And the claim of “about one million more participants and 600 more events” than in October makes the whole thing sound like a carefully amplified show of momentum. I’d be wary of treating it as spontaneous proof of what the country thinks; mass dissent can be managed and packaged just as easily as it can be genuine.

output.main_topic: Unverified turnout figures and framing of the “No Kings” events
subtopics: Skepticism about interpreting turnout as public opinion

central_relations.subject: the claim
central_relations.object: more participants and more events than in October

output.narrative_frame: Skeptical framing of organiser-reported turnout as unverified and potentially amplified.
opinions: The gap between organiser figures and the absence of an official count helps project overwhelming opposition.
